figure_caption: Fixed-resource mean inference for the population mean using an externally frozen scalar score. For each outer fold, only the training complement supplies normalization, calibration, finite-N scaling, and three-fold paired-risk selection; its held-out labels supply the residual correction. Unlabeled score values never enter fitting or selection: only their sample size enters the training size ratio. All fitted fold controls are evaluated on one shared unlabeled pool, and the variance of their weighted sum retains shared-pool covariance. The evaluated ordinary return is a Student-based asymptotic interval, with binary clipping and the specified label-only fallbacks. Its repeated-sampling assessment is not a coverage certificate. The binary-only internal bounded construction is computed but not returned and supplies no radius to the returned interval. Learned-control asymptotics require additional stability and moment assumptions not verified by selection; neither an exact binomial fallback nor any arrow certifies coverage of the full procedure.

panels.title: Fixed-resource mean inference
panels.short_caption: Training-only control selection, held-out mean correction, and shared-pool studentization form one evaluated return path; a separate unreturned binary bound is not its coverage certificate.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: a fixed-resource population-mean estimator learns score controls strictly behind a training boundary, corrects them on held-out labels and a single shared unlabeled pool, and returns an asymptotic interval rather than the separately computed internal bound. Draw one connected schematic, not multiple independent mini-panels. It occupies a full-width 21:9 canvas. All algorithmic operations and data must be native drawio shapes; there are no plots, deferred artwork, numeric results, or invented observations. Do not assign colors or palette.

REGIONS AND NODES, WITH STABLE IDS AND SEMANTIC ROLES. resource_region is an enclosing bracket or open container for fixed inputs, labeled 'Fixed resources'; no trainable operation lives here. frozen_f is a frozen, sharp annotation box labeled 'Frozen predictor f', with a small lock glyph made from native shapes if desired; it denotes score provenance, not an updateable model and not a source of outcome labels. target is a plain annotation 'Population mean' with the symbol theta on the same line. resource_note is the plain noun phrase 'Same inputs across methods'. labeled is a sharp data box labeled 'Labeled pairs' and '(Y_i, P_i), n'. pool is ONE cylinder labeled 'Shared unlabeled scores' and 'U_j, N'. Do not duplicate this cylinder anywhere. checks is a fixed decision diamond labeled 'Fallback checks'; it checks constant scores in either pool and binary counts. split is a fixed process rounded box labeled 'Outer folds'. train_data is a sharp data box labeled 'Training complement'. heldout is a sharp data box labeled 'Held-out fold I_k'. ratio is a small fixed auxiliary rounded box labeled 'Size ratio' and rho.

training_region is a clear enclosing container labeled 'Training only', containing train_data, candidate_menu, inner_region, refit, and ratio. Its right/bottom boundary must be conspicuous and visibly separate it from heldout and all held-out inference operations. candidate_menu is a sharp three-cell candidate-data box with cells zero_candidate 'Zero' (fixed control), affine_candidate 'Affine' (trainable family), and nonlinear_candidate 'Nonlinear' (trainable ridge-basis family). Do not redraw three full estimator pipelines. inner_region is a nested grouping labeled 'Three-fold inner validation', containing inner_fit (trainable rounded process, 'Fit + finite-N scaling') and select (fixed selection-rule rounded process, 'Paired-risk selection'). Inner fitting learns calibration parameters and signed scaling on inner training subsets; the inner validation criterion uses residual variability plus the finite-unlabeled-size penalty. select compares paired fold risks with their standard error, not a significance-test badge. refit is a trainable rounded process labeled 'Outer-training refit'. controls is a sharp result/data box just OUTSIDE the training boundary labeled 'Fold control g_k', with a small plain tag 'Fixed for inference'. It represents the collection of trained outer-fold controls; their upstream provenance remains learned, not an externally fixed oracle. fold_note is a plain annotation next to the boundary 'Each outer fold k'.

correction_region is an open grouping below the training region labeled 'Held-out correction'. apply_labeled is a frozen-at-inference rounded process labeled 'Score-control evaluation'. subtract is a native subtraction junction with one positive input for Y_i and one negative input for the control evaluation; its only interior label is the minus glyph. residual_moments is a fixed rounded process labeled 'Within-fold moments' with a short r_i symbol. residual_sum is a weighted-summation primitive, not an equation box, labeled 'Weighted residual mean'.

shared_region is an open grouping to the right of the fold-specific operations labeled 'One shared pool'. apply_pool is a frozen-at-inference rounded process labeled 'Shared-pool evaluation'; all g_k are evaluated on exactly the same U_j. control_sum is a weighted-summation primitive labeled 'Weighted control sum H'; aggregation is per observation BEFORE either moment calculation. pool_moments is a fixed rounded process labeled 'Shared-pool moments'. Do not draw separate foldwise unlabeled variance nodes or fictitious independent pools.

return_region is an open grouping at the right labeled 'Evaluated return path'. estimate is a native plus junction labeled only with a plus glyph; its output is the point estimate theta-hat. studentizer is a fixed rounded process labeled 'Shared-pool studentizer' with the single symbol V-hat. student_interval is a fixed rounded process labeled 'Student interval' with a small plain tag 'Binary clipping'. returned is the primary sharp result box labeled 'Returned interval'. ordinary_tag is the plain noun phrase 'Asymptotic branch' next to student_interval, not a certificate stamp. fallback is a fixed rounded process labeled 'Label-only fallback', with two short lines 'Binary: Clopper-Pearson' and 'Real: Student'. It connects to the same returned result, not to the internal bound. fallback_note is a compact plain note beside checks with exactly the two lines 'Constant scores' and 'Binary: <10 successes/failures'; the second condition is binary-only, explained in the caption rather than a long canvas sentence. certificate_note is a prominent plain caution immediately below returned, labeled 'No coverage certificate'. This caution applies to the full selected rule, not just one branch.

internal_region is a visibly separate dashed-outline auxiliary container in the lower-right margin, labeled 'Internal binary bound'. bounds is a fixed rounded process inside it labeled 'Foldwise bounded radii'; bounded_result is a sharp auxiliary result box inside it labeled 'Unreturned radius'. This region has no outgoing edge to any other region. The binary construction is a different object, not another option in the returned-interval decision.

EVERY EDGE. Solid arrows mean forward data flow or selected return flow. Dashed arrows mean auxiliary sample-size information or inputs to the unreturned computation, never gradients or proof implications. The following is the complete edge inventory; do not add certificate, oracle, predictor-update, or evaluation-result arrows. labeled -> checks, solid, no label; pool -> checks, solid, no label, routed outside the training container. checks -> split, solid, label 'Otherwise'; checks -> fallback, solid, label 'Triggered'. split -> train_data and split -> heldout, solid, no labels. labeled -> ratio, dashed, label 'n'; pool -> ratio, dashed, label 'N only', entering through a narrow sample-size-only port at the training boundary. candidate_menu -> inner_fit, solid, no label; train_data -> inner_fit, solid, no label; inner_fit -> select, solid, label 'Validation risks'; ratio -> inner_fit and ratio -> select, dashed, no labels. select -> refit, solid, label 'Selected family'; train_data -> refit, solid, no label; ratio -> refit, dashed, no label; refit -> controls, solid, no label, crossing the training boundary once. heldout -> apply_labeled, solid, label P_i; controls -> apply_labeled, solid, no label; heldout -> subtract, solid, label Y_i, into the positive port; apply_labeled -> subtract, solid, no label, into the negative port. subtract -> residual_moments, solid, no label. residual_moments -> residual_sum, solid, label w_k; residual_sum -> estimate, solid, no label. controls -> apply_pool and pool -> apply_pool, solid, no labels; apply_pool -> control_sum, solid, label w_k; control_sum -> pool_moments, solid, no label. pool_moments -> estimate, solid, label 'Mean'. residual_moments -> studentizer, solid, label 'Within-fold variances'; pool_moments -> studentizer, solid, label 'Variance'. estimate -> student_interval, solid, label theta-hat; studentizer -> student_interval, solid, label V-hat; student_interval -> returned, solid, no label; fallback -> returned, solid, label 'Fallback'. controls -> bounds, dashed, label 'Control bounds'; subtract -> bounds, dashed, no label; apply_pool -> bounds, dashed, no label; bounds -> bounded_result, solid, no label, entirely inside internal_region. frozen_f, target, resource_note, fold_note, fallback_note, ordinary_tag, and certificate_note are non-flow annotations without edges. There is absolutely no heldout -> training arrow and no unlabeled score-value arrow into training. All flows through train_data are interpreted foldwise, not as permanently disjoint global training and test datasets.

SPATIAL LAYOUT. Prefer one broad left-to-right backbone with two parallel middle lanes. Put fixed resources and the fold split at the left. Put training complement, candidate menu, inner fitting/selection and outer refit across the upper-middle lane, with g_k at its outward boundary. Put held-out data, score-control evaluation, residual subtraction and residual moments in a lower-middle lane, separated from the training container. Place the ONE pool cylinder above/right of these lanes with unobstructed routes to shared-pool evaluation, its weighted control sum, and moments. Converge weighted residual mean and shared-pool mean at the point-estimate plus glyph. Align the studentizer underneath that glyph and route both outputs into Student interval and then Returned interval at the right. Route the fallback as a compact bypass along the outer lower edge to the same Returned interval. Keep the separate internal binary-bound region below shared-pool/studentization operations; dashed auxiliary inputs approach its upper/left edges, while its result stops inside. Reserve generous whitespace at the training boundary and between Returned interval and Unreturned radius. Orthogonal connectors and distinct labeled ports must make data provenance and mean-versus-variance branches unambiguous; avoid long edges through process interiors. The outer-fold indication is a compact annotation, not K repeated diagrams. If the single container cannot accommodate a long label on one line, use a deliberate two-line short name, not smaller type or omitted structure.

IMPORTANCE. First: fixed resources and population-mean target, the held-out training boundary, and the dominant Returned interval versus disconnected Unreturned radius. Second: one shared pool, aggregation before variance, the two mean inputs to the plus glyph, and the studentizer's two variance inputs. Third: inner candidate families, finite-N sample-size-only port, and fallback bypass. Use no checkmarks, shields, seals, confidence badges, results bars, error bars, or numerical performance claims.

EXACT TEXT BUDGET. Only the node, region, annotation, and edge labels enumerated above may appear, with math rendered natively via MathJax where useful. Render symbols theta, rho, I_k, g_k, r_i, w_k, P_i, Y_i, U_j, n, N, theta-hat, and V-hat as symbols rather than spelled-out words. For the three subcells use only Zero / Affine / Nonlinear; no coefficients or basis equations. Sum and subtraction operations must use their native junction primitives, never multi-term equation boxes. There are ZERO raw multi-term equations in this figure. Do not draw an additional title inside the canvas, source citations, letter sublabels, explanatory sentences, proof assumptions, outcome counts, or evaluation metrics. Mechanism details and qualifications belong in the supplied caption, not expanded on-canvas prose.
